intro_html: A proper chowder is potatoes, dairy and something smoky, and this one checks all three boxes before the turkey even shows up. Bacon renders down, potatoes go soft enough to thicken the pot on their own, sweet corn adds pop, and a few dashes of hot sauce at the end wakes the whole thing up. Thick, filling, and built almost entirely out of the cheapest aisles in the store.
cost_closing_html: About $2.41 a bowl for a thick, bacon-smoked chowder. Potatoes and canned corn are two of the cheapest things you can buy, and here they are doing most of the heavy lifting.
shop_smart: Buy potatoes in the big bag. This chowder leans on them hard, and the per pound price on an eight or ten pound bag is a fraction of what loose potatoes cost.
Canned corn beats frozen for a chowder. It is cheaper, it is already soft, and the liquid in the can can go right into the pot instead of down the drain.
Bacon is the flavor engine, so a little goes far. Render it first, cook everything else in that fat, and you get smoke through the entire pot from a quarter pound.
Turkey breast is the one line worth shopping. Buy a frozen roast when the holiday price hits, cook it, and freeze it pulled and portioned for chowders and soups all winter.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Chop the bacon and render it in your big pot with the olive oil until crisp. Lift the bacon out and leave the fat.
Add the butter, then the diced onion and celery, and cook until soft. Stir in the garlic for the last minute.
Sprinkle the flour over the vegetables and stir for two minutes so it loses the raw taste and coats everything.
Pour in the chicken broth while stirring, add the peeled and cubed potatoes, and simmer until the potatoes are fork tender and starting to break down.
Add the drained corn and the cooked turkey breast and bring it back to a simmer.
Stir in the heavy cream and the hot sauce, warm it through without boiling, then season with salt and black pepper and scatter the reserved bacon back on top.
portion_html: Set the full pot on your scale and subtract the empty pot weight from Step 1. Divide by 14 and ladle that exact weight into each container. Every bowl lands near 581 calories with 36 grams of protein. Potato chowders thicken hard in the fridge, so a splash of broth on reheat brings it right back.
upsell_html: A thick, smoky chowder for about $2.41 a bowl. This is one of many. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons, calculators, and tools, all for $1 a month.

head.description: Bacon, potatoes, sweet corn and turkey breast in a thick creamy chowder. A 14 serving cold weather batch portioned by weight for meal prep.
head.keywords: turkey corn chowder, leftover turkey recipe, potato corn chowder, budget meal prep, cheap soup recipe, bacon chowder
steps: Render the chopped bacon in the pot, remove it, and keep the fat.
Cook the onion, celery and garlic in the fat and butter, then dust with flour.
Add the chicken broth and cubed potatoes and simmer until the potatoes break down.
Stir in the corn and cooked turkey breast and return to a simmer.
Finish with heavy cream and hot sauce, season, and top with the bacon.
